description:
kith-peer/src/lib.rs Peer/deliver handler (step 2, line 187) requires identity.user_id == msg.sender_user_id before any DB write. Combined with the WhoIs-based identity in the extractor, this means a peer cannot deliver a message claiming to be from someone else: the transport identity and the claimed sender must match.

This is the anti-spoof mechanism described in the architecture doc. It requires no signatures, no PKI, no challenge-response — just a structural invariant that the verified Tailscale caller identity must equal the senderUserId field.

Worth defending if someone suggests removing the check as 'redundant with auth' (it is not: auth verifies the caller is a known permitted peer; this check verifies the caller is the same person they claim to be in the message payload). The empty identity.user_id guard (line 181) prevents the degenerate case where an empty string matches an empty stored sender_user_id.
title: DECISION: senderUserId anti-spoof check at Peer/deliver boundary
